tests.name: Real paid subscription activates only after signed webhook
Concurrent duplicate signed webhook is idempotent
Public checkout remains locked
Real Buy More Checkout Session created without premature grant
Real browser Buy More payment grants once only after signed webhook
Real auto-top-up payment, exactly-once grant, concurrency and monthly cap
Real prorated upgrade activates through webhook
Real scheduled downgrade executes at renewal
Real renewal payment grants a fresh included period
Real failed renewal starts fixed grace; application clock boundary enforces read-only
Real renewal recovery restores operational access
Real browser pricing, signup, verified email handoff, Stripe payment and entitlement
Tenant isolation blocks a foreign inventory purchase
Real failed upgrade does not revoke an already-paid tier
Real failed upgrade recovers after successful payment and signed activation
Out-of-order genuine webhook retries reconcile after subscription ownership
Real authentication-required auto-top-up grants no usage and cannot repeatedly charge
Real won dispute adjusts purchased funding through signed events
Real lost dispute adjusts purchased funding through signed events
Real purchased-pack refund is recorded exactly once and spent funding is flagged
Actual Stripe invoice payments and balance-transaction fees reconciled
No unresolved Stripe fee, payment-binding or delivery warnings

notes: Stripe CLI device authorization was approved by the user for this sandbox only; credentials remained in Stripe's credential store.
Real renewal invoices were collected; application grace expiry was evaluated using an injected evaluation timestamp, not by waiting seven real days.
Email verification used the local encrypted outbox; external email delivery was not tested.
14 actual Stripe balance fee rows reconciled; no missing Stripe fee/payment-binding/delivery/attribution warnings remained.
REFUNDED_SPENT_USAGE was deliberately triggered by the spent-refund scenario.
Missing provider cost rates and infrastructure coverage still block commercial readiness and pricing approval.
